opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. As the role owning the Payroll system, admin is permitted for full-time employees. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E013 shows contractor with basic security training (not full-time as previously noted). Per policy, contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The security note indicates Jesse Stewart (E013) is a contractor with basic security training, correcting the earlier note. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and admin is never permitted. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum allowed level (read), the final access granted is read.

content.text:
There are two conflicting notes. One says full-time Payroll Specialist, admin permitted. The other says contractor with basic training, max read, recommend read.

The Security note appears to correct the earlier note (contractor, basic training). Security record should be authoritative, presumably. The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. So max for contractor with basic training is read.

Requested admin. Above max, grant max = read.

I'll submit read.
